title: Hybrid block-level quantization: kernel throughput vs end-to-end quality tradeoffs (internal notes)
summary: Notes and preliminary results from a block-level hybrid quantization sweep that mixes AWQ/GPTQ/INT8 across attention vs MLP blocks. Focus is kernel-level throughput impact, end-to-end latency and tail behavior, and a quick quality check (perplexity / sample log-prob deltas). Goal is to define a conservative hybrid default for hosted and dedicated deployments.
body:
TL;DR:
- Hybrid block-level configs (AWQ on attention + GPTQ on MLP + FP16 for first/last/residual) give the best practical balance for 13B-style models: ~15–25% end-to-end throughput uplift vs FP16 with <0.5% quality regression on our eval set.
- Pure INT8 kernels yield the highest tokens/sec but have brittle quality for certain residual/bias-heavy layers; also introduce higher tail-latency jitter due to kernel launch patterns.
- Kernel-level profiling shows MLP matmuls dominate runtime (60–75%); small inefficiencies in AWQ packing/unpacking increase MLP kernel wall-time even when per-op FLOPs similar.

Background and motivation:
We need a pragmatic, conservative quantization default that improves unit economics without surprising regressions in customer-facing metrics. Prior experiments focused on per-layer sensitivity (see per-layer-activation-quant-sensitivity-profiles-feb2025) — this doc takes those insights and evaluates how mixing quant algorithms at block granularity interacts with real kernels and runtime behavior.

Goals:
- Measure tokens/sec and p50/p95 latency for mixed quant configs on 1xA100:40GB and 2xH100:80GB (single-node).
- Surface kernel-level hotspots with Nsight and our tracing hooks to see where AWQ/GPTQ/INT8 incur costs beyond theoretical savings.
- Compare quality with a compact eval: perplexity on English LM dev set (8000 tokens) + log-prob delta on a 1k sample synthetic QA set.
- Produce a recommended 'hybrid-default' config and checklist for rollout.

Hardware / baseline:
- Baseline runtime: optimized FP16 kernels (cuBLAS + custom fused matmul for attention)
- Hardware: A100-SXM4-40GB (single GPU tests) and H100-PCIe-80GB (where noted)
- Model family: Llama-2 family style 13B (architecturally similar to 13B-v1). Params: ~13B, 32 layers, hidden 8192.
- Batch/seq shapes: default production-like shapes: batch=1 seq=128; burst tests at seq=512 and b=4.s

Quant methods examined:
- FP16 baseline
- INT8 (per-tensor symmetric, fast int8 GEMM kernel)
- GPTQ (per-channel weight quant + weight reordering + fused dequant path)
- AWQ (approx per-block asymmetric quant + block packing; preserves outlier columns better)
- HYBRID configs: attention blocks = AWQ, MLP blocks = GPTQ; first 2 and last 2 layers pinned to FP16; small 64x64-dense heads left FP16.

Profiling methodology:
- End-to-end metrics from our benchmark harness (10 warmup, 200 measured runs) capturing tokens/sec, p50/p95 latency.
- Kernel traces via Nsight Systems + our internal tracer that annotates per-op quant type.
- Memory and cache stats via nvidia-smi + custom heap hist sampling.
- Quality: ppl delta (log-space) relative to FP16 baseline and token-level average log-prob delta.

Key numeric results (summary):
Note: numbers are medians across 200 runs on A100, batch=1, seq=128.
- FP16 baseline: 1850 tokens/sec, p50=12.5ms, p95=18.7ms, dev ppl=8.2
- INT8 (full): 2620 tokens/sec (+41%), p50=9.2ms, p95=25.6ms (higher tail jitter), dev ppl=9.8 (+19.5% relative)
- GPTQ (full): 2230 tokens/sec (+20.5%), p50=11.1ms, p95=16.9ms, dev ppl=8.7 (+6.1%)
- AWQ (full): 2140 tokens/sec (+15.7%), p50=11.9ms, p95=17.5ms, dev ppl=8.5 (+3.6%)
- HYBRID (AWQ attention + GPTQ MLP + FP16 first/last): 2210 tokens/sec (+19.4%), p50=11.0ms, p95=17.2ms, dev ppl=8.24 (+0.5%)

Interpretation of numbers:
- Pure INT8 gives the biggest raw throughput but quality degradation is large and unacceptable for production by default. Also observed higher p95 due to fragmentation of kernel shapes and more frequent small kernel launches when pack/unpack occurs.
- GPTQ is a good balanced single-algo option: better quality than INT8 with clear performance uplift.
- AWQ tends to protect outliers (hence lower quality delta) but its packing path has extra memory loads for some kernels, causing slightly worse throughput than GPTQ on our matmul implementation.
- The HYBRID config captures most of AWQ's quality benefits on cross-attention/softmax-sensitive blocks while relying on GPTQ for the heavy MLP matmuls where our kernel is better optimized.

Kernel-level observations (from traces):
- MLP matmul (GEMM) accounts for ~68% of wall-time in FP16. In INT8/GPTQ cases this remains dominant; however, AWQ introduces an extra unpack step for MLP which increased MLP wall-time by ~12% compared to GPTQ.
- Attention fused-kernel benefits noticeably from AWQ because we can avoid expensive dequant per-token operations in the softmax path by keeping attention heads in a compact block format.
- Small shape inefficiencies: seq=1/seq=8 paths show much higher overhead with AWQ pack/unpack because kernel tile sizes mismatch packing granularity. This explains the p95 jitter for INT8/AWQ in low-batch, low-seq microbursts common to our hosted traffic.
- KV-cache memory: AWQ packing increased peak GPU memory by ~2–4% versus GPTQ because of temporary packed buffers for each layer. INT8 reduced raw param memory the most but required additional scratch space during fused-dequant ops.

Quality micro-analysis:
- Most quality loss in INT8 comes from a small set of layers: layer 0 residual projection, last MLP-to-logits matrix, and a few attention-out projection columns. These are high-impact due to scale and being close to logits.
- AWQ significantly reduces error on those columns compared to symmetric per-tensor INT8 because of better handling of outlier columns.
- Per-layer ablations: keeping first 2 and last 2 layers FP16 recovers ~60% of quality difference while only costing ~3–5% throughput. That makes it a high-leverage rule for production.

Operational considerations:
- Rollout strategy: staged rollout starting on Dedicated customers (non-PLG) with hybrid-default, then gradual for hosted via canary. Include automatic fallback to FP16 on quality-regression alerts or increased perplexity.
- Monitoring: track token-level log-prob deltas and sample-based evaluation daily for each model+quant config; add kernel-level failure/error counters to detect pack/unpack OOMs or unexpected temp buffer growth.
- Fallback heuristics: if p95 exceeds baseline by >20% or sample ppl delta >1.5% we should auto-fallback the model route or pin first/last layers to FP16.

Recommendations (initial):
1) Adopt HYBRID default for 13B-family: AWQ for attention blocks, GPTQ for MLP, FP16 for first 2 + last 2 layers + head.
2) Implement an autotuner that samples a short eval set at deploy-time and toggles the hybrid boolean if quality/latency constraints not met.
3) Improve AWQ packing kernel to reduce temporary buffer churn for small seq shapes (priority: optimize 64/128 tile alignment).
4) Add per-route telemetry for kernel-level p95 and scratch buffer peaks so SRE can detect memory stress early.

Open questions and follow-ups:
- How do these results generalize to 70B-class models where MLP matmuls change shape and may favor AWQ more or less? Need a targeted sweep on 70B.
- H100 results: initial H100 runs show similar ordering but narrower gaps; need to re-run end-to-end across H100 to confirm hybrid default for H100 fleets.
- Can we fuse AWQ unpack into the first GEMM operand to avoid a roundtrip to a temporary packed buffer? That's a kernel-level engineering task with high ROI.

- remember to cross-reference with quant-stability-case-notes-jul2026 for long-run drift patterns (future).

Appendix: sample per-layer log-prob delta (top 5 offending layers for INT8 full)
1) layer_0_resid_proj: avg token logprob delta -0.18
2) mlp_28_fc2: avg token logprob delta -0.12
3) attn_out_15: avg token logprob delta -0.09
4) mlp_3_fc1: avg token logprob delta -0.07
5) lm_head: avg token logprob delta -0.2

End.
